extracted.intended_audience: Public stakeholders in pesticide registration review (environmental and human health advocates; chemical industry; pesticide users; interested members of the public)
extracted.subtask_description: A Federal Register notice announcing availability of EPA's revised mitigation and response-to-comments memorandum for sulfuryl fluoride, explaining the legal authority, procedural posture, docket access, and how the public input and risk assessments are used in registration review and mitigation decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory standard for registration (FIFRA section 3(c)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Under FIFRA section 3(c)(5), a pesticide product may be registered or remain registered only if, when used in accordance with widespread and commonly recognized practice, the pesticide performs its intended function without unreasonable adverse effects on the environment; that is, without any unreasonable risk to man or the environment, or a human dietary risk from residues that result from the use of a pesticide in or on food.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the governing substantive standard EPA uses in registration review to determine whether a pesticide's registration should be maintained, revised, or mitigated. (Page cites 7 U.S.C. 136a(c)(5) and explains application in review.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration review periodicity (Section 3(g) of FIFRA)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA conducts registration review of pesticides pursuant to section 3(g) of FIFRA, which provides that registrations of pesticides are to be reviewed every 15 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice cites section 3(g) and the Procedural Regulations for Registration Review at 40 CFR part 155, subpart C as the legal basis and timetable for the program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of current scientific and other knowledge in review
rubrics_metrics.description: Through the registration review program, EPA ensures that each pesticide's registration is based on current scientific and other knowledge, including its effects on human health and the environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration review is meant to incorporate updated science and knowledge into decisions about whether pesticides meet the statutory standard; this underpins EPA's ability to pursue mitigation when new information indicates risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to pursue mitigation during review if unreasonable risks found
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA may pursue mitigation at any time during the registration review process if it finds that a pesticide poses unreasonable adverse effects to human health or the environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice explains EPA may implement mitigation before completion of the full review (as an 'early mitigation') and references 40 CFR 155.58 as the regulatory mechanism for announcing such actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public accessibility of registration review docket (40 CFR 155.58)
rubrics_metrics.description: As provided in 40 CFR 155.58, the registration review docket for each pesticide case will remain publicly accessible through the duration of the registration review process; that is, until all actions required in the final decision on the registration review case have been completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Docket is available online at regulations.gov and includes supporting documents (meeting minutes, data sheets, analyses). The notice provides the docket ID (EPA-HQ-OPP-2009-0136) and guidance on accessing documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public participation and solicitation of input on additional mitigation
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA will solicit public input on any additional risk mitigation in a Proposed Interim Decision (PID).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice documents that EPA issued a Draft Interim Re-Entry Mitigation Measures for public comment (May 2021), received comments that resulted in revisions (e.g., aeration procedures), and will use the PID process to seek further comment before additional mitigation is adopted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigation must address identified human health risks and OIG recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Sulfuryl Fluoride Revised Mitigation and Response to Comments memorandum is being issued to address human health concerns and in response to EPA's Office of Inspector General 2016 Report ('Additional Measures Can Be Taken to Prevent Deaths and Serious Injuries from Residential Fumigations').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA states mitigation measures outlined are necessary to address identified human health risk concerns from the use of sulfuryl fluoride as a structural fumigant; comments received resulted in changes to the Agency's mitigation decision (for example, revising aeration procedures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance of mitigation and continued availability
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA expects that implementation of the mitigation measures described in this risk mitigation document will allow sulfuryl fluoride products to remain available to users while addressing the recommendations from the OIG report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice frames mitigation as intended to reduce risks while preserving access to products when feasible — an explicit policy consideration in mitigation decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possibility of further mitigation after completion of all risk assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: Once all the risk assessments are completed for all the uses of sulfuryl fluoride, EPA may propose additional mitigation to address potential risks, as part of the normal registration review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This sets the expectation that early mitigation may be followed by further measures informed by complete risk assessments and subject to public notice-and-comment via a PID.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency through supporting documents in docket
rubrics_metrics.description: The registration review docket contains supporting documents (e.g., meeting minutes, secondary reviews, data sheets, calibration receipts) that informed the Agency's decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice lists example supporting documents and indicates there are 93 supporting documents available in the docket, underscoring the evidentiary basis and transparency requirements for the action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal authority and procedural citations as required elements of the notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The action cites its statutory and regulatory authority (e.g., 7 U.S.C. 136 et seq.; 40 CFR part 155, subpart C; 40 CFR 155.58) and includes standard Federal Register notice sections (AGENCY, ACTION, SUMMARY, ADDRESSES, FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT, SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice follows required format and cites authorities to establish the legal basis for the availability announcement and related procedural steps.
